title: Omni-Weather: A Unified Multimodal Model for Weather Radar Understanding and Generation
claim: One unified model covers diverse understanding and generation tasks and outperforms specialized baselines across all of them.
layout: Central radial bar chart surrounded by four task quadrants with chat examples
description: A rounded poster-style figure split into four pastel quadrants around a central circular radar-style bar chart titled "Omni-Weather". The quadrants are Radar Sequence Understanding (top-left, blue), Radar Inversion (top-right, green), Radar Nowcasting (bottom-right, yellow) and Radar Image Understanding (bottom-left, pink). Each quadrant has a cursive heading, radar image strips, and chat bubbles. Gray bubbles hold user prompts, with hacker avatars. Yellow or blue bubbles hold robot-avatar answers, with key phrases in orange or red. The inversion quadrant shows satellite infrared input and a generated VIL radar output. The nowcasting quadrant shows input and predicted frame sequences. The center ring holds grouped colored bars for several baselines and Omni-Weather on metrics such as CSI, SSIM, Accuracy and GPT4-score, with a legend at top. The eye goes first to the central title and ring.
caption: Illustration of Omni-Weather’s unified capabilities.
abstract: Weather modeling requires both accurate prediction and mechanistic interpretation, yet existing methods treat these goals in isolation, separating generation from understanding. To address this gap, we present Omni-Weather, the first multimodal foundation model that unifies weather generation and understanding within a single architecture. Omni-Weather integrates a radar encoder for weather generation tasks, followed by unified processing using a shared self-attention mechanism. Moreover, we construct a Chain-of-Thought dataset for causal reasoning in weather generation, enabling interpretable outputs and improved perceptual quality. Extensive experiments show Omni-Weather achieves state-of-the-art performance in both weather generation and understanding. Our findings further indicate that generative and understanding tasks in the weather domain can mutually enhance each other. Omni-Weather also demonstrates the feasibility and value of unifying weather generation and understanding.
